title: Inverse Entropic Optimal Transport Solves Semi-supervised Learning via Data Likelihood Maximization
claim: Compared with a prior method, ours translates source images into outputs that better match the target while preserving identity-relevant attributes.
layout: 4x4 image grid, columns Source/Target/baseline/Ours, left-to-right reading
description: A 4-row by 4-column grid of face photographs with tight borders and no arrows. Column headers, partly cropped at the top, read Source, Target, FSBM and Ours. Each row starts with a woman's face as the source. The next column shows the paired ground-truth man's face as the target. The third column shows the FSBM baseline output, and the fourth shows the output from the proposed method. Across the rows, the subjects vary in ethnicity, age and background. The eye is drawn across each row to compare the last two columns against the target. The proposed method's outputs look closer to the target in pose, hair and facial hair, with fewer artifacts than FSBM.
caption: Semi-supervised Woman-to-Man Translation: A comparison between FSBM (Theodoropoulos et al., 2024) and our method. Both methods are applied within the ALAE latent space (Pidhorskyi et al., 2020) using 1024×1024 FFHQ images (Karras et al., 2019). See M5.3 for further experimental details.
abstract: Learning conditional distributions $Ï^*(\cdot|x)$ is a central problem in machine learning, which is typically approached via supervised methods with paired data $(x,y) \sim Ï^*$. However, acquiring paired data samples is often challenging, especially in problems such as domain translation. This necessitates the development of $\textit{semi-supervised}$ models that utilize both limited paired data and additional unpaired i.i.d. samples $x \sim Ï^*_x$ and $y \sim Ï^*_y$ from the marginal distributions. The usage of such combined data is complex and often relies on heuristic approaches. To tackle this issue, we propose a new learning paradigm called $\textbf{EBiEOT}$ that integrates both paired and unpaired data seamlessly using data likelihood maximization techniques. We demonstrate that our approach also connects intriguingly with inverse entropic optimal transport (OT). This finding allows us to apply recent advances in computational OT to establish an $\textit{end-to-end}$ learning algorithm to get $Ï^*(\cdot|x)$. In addition, we derive the universal approximation property, demonstrating that our approach can theoretically recover true conditional distributions with arbitrarily small error. Finally, we demonstrate through empirical tests that our method effectively learns conditional distributions using paired and unpaired data simultaneously. The code of $\texttt{EBiEOT}$ is available at https://github.com/MuXauJl11110/EBiEOT.
